Consumer Liability and Error Resolution Liability of Consumers for Unauthorized Transfers – 12 CFR 1005.6 A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized EFT (defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(m)) depending on when the consumer notifies the financial institution and whether an access device was used to conduct the transaction. Under the EFTA, there is no bright-line time limit within which consumers must report unauthorized EFTs (71 Fed. Reg. 1638, 1653 (Jan. 10, 2006)). The extent of the consumer’s liability is determined solely by the consumer’s promptness in notifying the financial institution (Comment 1005.6(b)-3). Other factors may not be used as a basis to hold consumers liable. Regulation E expressly prohibits the following factors as the basis for imposing greater liability than is permissible under Regulation E: the consumer was negligent (e.g., wrote a PIN on an ATM card); an agreement between the consumer and the financial institution provides for greater liability; or the consumer is liable for a greater amount under state law (Comments 1005.6(b)-2 and 1005.6(b)-3). A consumer may only be held liable for an unauthorized transaction, within the limitations set forth in 12 CFR 1005.6(b), if: • The financial institution has provided all of the following written disclosures to the consumer: o A summary of the consumer’s liability for unauthorized EFTs. o The telephone number and address for reporting that an unauthorized EFT has been or may be made. o The financial institution’s business days. • Any access device used to affect the EFT was an accepted access device (as defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(a)). • The financial institution has provided a means to identify the consumer to whom the access device was issued (12 CFR 1005.6(a)). Regulation E allows, but does not require, the financial institution to provide a separate means to identify each consumer of a multiple-user account (Comment 1005.6(a)-2). The limitations on the amount of consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs, the time limits within which consumers must report unauthorized EFTs, and the liability for failing to adhere to CFPB Manual V.2 (October 2012) EFTA 21"}, {"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001", "source": "title_12_part_1005_2026-11-03.xml", "page": "", "rrf_score": 0.029906956136464335, "text": "(a) Conditions for liability. A consumer may be held liable, within the limitations described in paragraph (b) of this section, for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer involving the consumer's account only if the financial institution has provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3). If the unauthorized transfer involved an access device, it must be an accepted access device and the financial institution must have provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued. (b) Limitations on amount of liability. A consumer's liability for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer or a series of related unauthorized transfers shall be determined as follows: (1) Timely notice given. If the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution. (2) Timely notice not given. If the consumer fails to notify the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $500 or the sum of: (i) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur within the two business days, whichever is less; and (ii) The amount of unauthorized transfers that occur after the close of two business days and before notice to the institution, provided the institution establishes that these transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified the institution within that two-day period. (3) Periodic statement; timely notice not given. A consumer must report an unauthorized electronic fund transfer that appears on a periodic statement within 60 days of the financial institution's transmittal of the statement to avoid liability for subsequent transfers. If the consumer fails to do so, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the amount of the unauthorized transfers that occur after the close of the 60 days and before notice to the institution, and that the institution establishes would not have occurred had the consumer notified the institution within the 60-day period. Even if the consumer is unable to provide the account number or the card number, the notice effectively limits the consumer’s liability if the consumer sufficiently identifies the account in question, for example, by giving the name on the account and the type of account (Comment 1005.6(b)(5)-3).                                                                                                  # Initial Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n## Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made involving the consumer's account** [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001].\n\n**Key timing rules and exceptions:**\n\n- Disclosures given earlier than required (e.g., when a consumer opens a checking account) need not be repeated when the consumer later authorizes an electronic check conversion or agrees with a third party to initiate preauthorized transfers, **unless the terms and conditions differ** from those previously disclosed [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001].\n- Where the agreement for EFT services is directly between the consumer and the account-holding institution, disclosures must be given **in close proximity to the event requiring disclosure** (e.g., when the consumer contracts for a new service) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001].\n- Where a consumer authorizes a third party to debit or credit the account and the institution has not received advance notice, the institution must provide disclosures **as soon as reasonably possible after the first debit or credit**, unless previously given [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001].\n- If a consumer opens a new account permitting EFTs and has already received Regulation E disclosures for another account at the same institution, the institution **need only disclose terms and conditions that differ** from those previously given [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001].\n- If a financial institution joins an interchange or shared network, disclosures are required for additional EFT services not previously available if the terms and conditions differ from those previously disclosed [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0002].\n\n---\n\n## Required Content of Initial Disclosures (12 CFR 1005.7(b))\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided **as applicable** [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]:\n\n### 1. Consumer Liability for Unauthorized Transfers\nA summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6, or under state or other applicable law or agreement, for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution does not need to provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability in the future [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001].\n\n### 2. Telephone Number and Address\nThe telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized EFT has been or may be made. A **specific** telephone number and address must be provided for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001].\n\n### 3. Business Days\nThe financial institution's business days [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001].\n\n### 4. Types of Transfers and Limitations on Frequency or Dollar Amount\nThe types of EFTs the consumer may make and any limitations on the frequency and dollar amount of transfers. Limitations generally must be disclosed in detail; however, **if confidentiality of certain details is essential to the security of an account or system, those details may be withheld**, but the existence of limitations must still be disclosed. A limitation on account activity that restricts the consumer's ability to make EFTs must be disclosed even if the restriction also applies to non-electronic transfers [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001].\n\n### 5. Fees\nAny fees imposed by the financial institution for EFTs or for the right to make transfers. A per-item fee must be disclosed even if the same fee applies to non-electronic transfers. If a fee applies only under certain conditions, those conditions must be disclosed [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0687_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001].\n\n### 6. Documentation\nA summary of the consumer's right to receipts and periodic statements (under § 1005.9), and notices regarding preauthorized transfers (under § 1005.10(a) and (d)) [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0687_chunk_0001].\n\n### 7.         # Periodic Statement Requirements Under Regulation E\n\n## 1. General Frequency Requirement\n\nFinancial institutions must send periodic statements:\n- **For each monthly cycle in which an EFT has occurred**, and\n- **At least quarterly** if no EFT has occurred during a cycle [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0703_chunk_0001].\n\n---\n\n## 2. Required Content of Periodic Statements\n\nFor each EFT made during the cycle, the periodic statement must include, as applicable [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0703_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002]:\n\n**Transaction Information (per EFT):**\n- Amount of the transfer (charges imposed at an electronic terminal by the terminal owner/operator may be included in the amount)\n- Date the transfer was posted to the account\n- Type of transfer(s) and type of account(s) to or from which funds were transferred\n- For each transfer (except deposits of cash or check/draft/similar paper instrument to the consumer's account) initiated at an electronic terminal: the terminal location as required for receipts under 12 CFR 1005.9(a)(5)\n- Name of any third-party payee or payor\n\n**Account-Level Information:**\n- Account number(s) [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002]\n- Total amount of any fees and charges (other than a finance charge as defined by Regulation Z) assessed during the period for making EFTs, the right to make EFTs, or for account maintenance [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0703_chunk_0001]\n- Balance in the account at the **beginning and close** of the statement period [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002]\n- Address and telephone number to be used by the consumer for inquiries or notice of errors (may appear on an accompanying abbreviated error notice) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0703_chunk_0001]\n- If the financial institution uses the telephone-notice option under 12 CFR 1005.10(a)(1)(iii): a telephone number the consumer may call to ascertain whether preauthorized transfers to the account have occurred [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n## 3. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement\n\n### a. Passbook Accounts\nWhere a consumer's passbook account may **only** be accessed by preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, **provided** the financial institution either:\n- Updates the passbook upon presentation (listing the amount and date of each EFT since the passbook was last presented), **or**\n- Provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer's request [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002].\n\n### b. Other Accounts Accessed Only by Preauthorized Transfers\nFor accounts (other than passbook accounts) that may be accessed **only** by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement **at least quarterly** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002].\n\n### c. Intra-Institutional Transfers\nIf an EFT is initiated by the consumer between **two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution**, documenting the transfer on a periodic statement for **one** of the two accounts satisfies the periodic statement requirement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002].\n\n> **Note:** An account accessed by both preauthorized transfers to the account and intra-institutional transfers, but by no other type of EFT, qualifies for the preauthorized-transfer exception (not the intra-institutional exception) [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002].\n\n### d. Foreign-Initiated Transfers\nIf an EFT is **initiated outside the United States**, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer, **provided** it treats any inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error under 12 CFR 1005.11 [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002].\n\n---\n\n## 4. Alternative to Periodic Statements for Payroll Card Accounts (12 CFR 1005.18)\n\nA financial institution offering **payroll card accounts** need not furnish periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b) if it makes available to the consumer all of the following [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0002] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. The **account balance**, through a readily available telephone line\n2. An **electronic history** of account transactions covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account\n3. A **written history** of account transactions provided promptly in response to an oral or written request, covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the financial institution receives the consumer's request\n\nThe history of account transactions must include the same type of information required on periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001].\n\n### Compliance Obligations When Using the Payroll Card Alternative:\n- **Modify initial disclosures** under 12 CFR 1005.7(b) to disclose: the telephone number for balance inquiries, the means to obtain electronic account history, and a summary of the right to receive a written account history upon request [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n- **Provide an annual error resolution notice** substantially similar to the model notice in Appendix A, paragraph A-7(b), in place of the standard annual notice under 12 CFR 1005.8(b) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n- **Liability limits:** For purposes of 12 CFR 1005.6(b)(3), the 60-day period for reporting unauthorized transfers begins on the earlier of the date the consumer electronically accesses the account (if the electronic history reflects the transfer) or the date the written history is provided [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n## 5. Alternative to Periodic Statements for Prepaid Accounts (12 CFR 1005.18 / Prepaid Rule)\n\nFor **prepaid accounts**, a financial institution need not furnish periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b) if it makes available [C:12CFR1005_1005.18_chunk_0020]:\n\n1. The consumer's **account balance** through a readily available telephone line\n2. An **electronic history** of account transactions covering at least **12 months** preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account\n3. A **written history** of account transactions provided promptly upon oral or written request, covering at least **24 months** preceding the date the financial institution receives the request\n\n> **Exception                                                                                                                                           [{"chunk_id": "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001", "source": "exam_manual_v2_2012.pdf", "page": "", "rrf_score": 0.03278688524590164, "text": "CFPB Consumer Laws and Regulations EFTA • If the financial institution has provided a telephone number which the consumer can use to find out whether or not a preauthorized transfer has taken place, that telephone number. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). For other accounts that may be accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)). • Transfers between accounts. If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2). Section 1005.3(c) of Regulation E describes transfers that are not EFTs and are therefore not covered by the EFTA and Regulation E: • Transfers of funds originated by check, draft, or similar paper instrument; • Check guarantee or authorization services that do not directly result in a debit or credit to a consumer’s account; • Any transfer of funds for a consumer within a system that is used primarily to transfer funds between financial institutions or businesses, e.g., Fedwire or other similar network; • Any transfer of funds which has as its primary purpose the purchase or sale of securities or commodities regulated by the SEC or the CFTC, purchased or sold through a broker-dealer regulated by the SEC or through a futures commission merchant regulated by the CFTC, or held in book-entry form by a Federal Reserve Bank or federal agency; • Intra-institutional automatic transfers under an agreement between a consumer and a financial institution; • Transfers initiated by telephone between a consumer and a financial institution provided the transfer is not a function of a written plan contemplating periodic or recurring transfers. # Periodic Statement Requirements Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.9)\n\n## 1. General Frequency Requirement\nFinancial institutions must send periodic statements for each monthly cycle in which an EFT has occurred, and at least quarterly if no EFT has occurred during a cycle (12 CFR 1005.9(b)).\n\n## 2. Required Content of Periodic Statements\nFor each EFT made during the cycle, the statement must include, as applicable (12 CFR 1005.9(b); exam manual):\n- Amount of the transfer (a terminal-owner/operator charge imposed at an electronic terminal may be included in the amount);\n- Date the transfer was posted to the account;\n- Type of transfer(s) and type of account(s) to or from which funds were transferred;\n- For each transfer (except deposits of cash, or a check/draft/similar paper instrument to the consumer's account) initiated at an electronic terminal, the terminal location as required for receipts under 1005.9(a)(5);\n- Name of any third-party payee or payor;\n- Account number(s);\n- Total amount of any fees and charges (other than a finance charge under Regulation Z) assessed during the period for making EFTs, the right to make EFTs, or for account maintenance;\n- Balance in the account at the beginning and close of the statement period;\n- Address and telephone number for inquiries or notice of errors (the address/telephone number on an error-resolution notice given on or with the statement satisfies this);\n- If the institution uses the telephone-notice option under 1005.10(a)(1)(iii), a telephone number the consumer may call to ascertain whether preauthorized transfers to the account have occurred.\n\n## 3. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement (1005.9(c)-(d))\n- **Passbook accounts** accessible only by preauthorized transfers to the account: no periodic statement needed if the institution updates the passbook upon presentation (listing amount and date of each EFT since last presented) or enters the information on a separate document (1005.9(c)(1)(i)).\n- **Other accounts** accessible only by preauthorized transfers to the account: statement required at least quarterly (1005.9(c)(1)(ii)).\n- **Intra-institutional transfers** between two accounts of the consumer at the same institution: documenting the transfer on a periodic statement for one of the two accounts satisfies the requirement (1005.9(c)(2)).\n- An account accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account and intra-institutional transfers (and no other EFT type) qualifies for the preauthorized-transfer exception under (c)(1) (1005.9(c)(3)).\n- **Foreign-initiated transfers**: no receipt or periodic statement needed if the transfer is not initiated within a state and the institution treats any inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error under 1005.11 (1005.9(d)).\n\n## 4. Payroll Card Account Alternative (12 CFR 1005.18(b))\nAn institution offering payroll card accounts need not furnish periodic statements under 1005.9(b) if it makes available:\n1. The account balance through a readily available telephone line;\n2. An electronic history covering at least 60 days preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account;\n3. A written history provided promptly on oral or written request covering at least 60 days preceding the request.\nThe histories must include the same information required on periodic statements under 1005.9(b). The institution must also modify initial disclosures under 1005.7(b), provide a substitute annual error-resolution notice (in place of 1005.8(b)), and apply the 60-day liability-reporting period for 1005.6(b)(3) beginning on the earlier of the date the consumer electronically accesses the account (if the history reflects the transfer) or the date the written history is provided.\n\n## 5. Prepaid Account Alternative (12 CFR 1005.18(c))\nAn institution need not furnish periodic statements under 1005.9(b) for prepaid accounts if it makes available:\n1. The account balance through a readily available telephone line;\n2. An electronic history covering at least 12 months preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account;\n3. A written history provided promptly on oral or written request covering at least 24 months preceding the request.\nThe histories must include the information set forth in 1005.9(b). Additionally:\n- For prepaid accounts that are not payroll card or government benefit accounts, the written history under (c)(1)(iii) is not required for any account for which the institution has not completed its consumer identification and verification process (1005.18(c)(2)).\n- The institution must disclose the amount of any fees assessed (whether for EFTs or otherwise) on any periodic statement and on any transaction history (1005.18(c)(4)).\n- The institution must display a summary total of all fees assessed for the prior calendar month and for the calendar year to date on any periodic statement and transaction history (1005.18(c)(5)).\n- The institution must comply with the modified disclosure requirements under 1005.18(d).\n\n(Note: Receipts, as distinct from periodic statements, are not required for EFTs of $15 or less under 1005.9(e).) us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED
      G3-05                                 What constitutes a billing error on an open-end credit account, and what must a creditor do after receiving a proper billing-error notice? ["12 CFR 1026.13"]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               ["12CFR1005_1005.33_chunk_0005", "12CFR1026_1026.6_chunk_0002", "12CFR1026_1026.6_chunk_0011", "12CFR1026_1026.8_chunk_0001", "12CFR1026_1026.12_chunk_0003", "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001", "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002", "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003", "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004", "12CFR1026_1026.54_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0140_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0423_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0478_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0485_chunk_0001"]        NaN ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts: Definition and Creditor Obligations\n\n### I. What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder 12 CFR § 1026.13(a), a **billing error** on an open-end credit account means any of the following seven categories [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — A charge reflected on or with a periodic statement for an extension of credit not made to the consumer or to a person with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan.\n\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — An extension of credit reflected on or with a periodic statement that is not identified in accordance with the requirements of §§ 1026.7(a)(2) or (b)(2) and 1026.8.\n\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — An extension of credit reflected on or with a periodic statement for property or services not accepted by the consumer or the consumer's designee, or not delivered to the consumer or the consumer's designee as agreed.\n\n4. **Failure to properly credit a payment** — A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account.\n\n5. **Computational or accounting error** — A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature made by the creditor.\n\n6. **Request for clarification** — A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence.\n\n7. **Failure to deliver a periodic statement** — The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received by the creditor in writing at least **20 days** before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### II. What Constitutes a Proper Billing-Error Notice\n\nA **billing error notice** must meet all three of the following requirements [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Timely receipt** — Received by the creditor at the address disclosed under § 1026.7(a)(9) or (b)(9) **no later than 60 days** after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement reflecting the alleged billing error.\n2. **Account identification** — Enables the creditor to identify the consumer's name and account number.\n3. **Description of error** — To the extent possible, indicates the consumer's belief and reasons for believing a billing error exists, and the type, date, and amount of the error.\n\n---\n\n### III. Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Proper Billing-Error Notice\n\n#### A. Acknowledgment and Resolution Deadlines\n\n- The creditor must **mail or deliver written acknowledgment** to the consumer **within 30 days** of receiving the billing error notice, unless the creditor has already completed the appropriate resolution procedures within that 30-day period. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]\n- The creditor must **complete the appropriate resolution procedures within 2 complete billing cycles, but in no event later than 90 days**, after receiving the billing error notice. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]\n\n#### B. Rules Pending Resolution\n\nUntil the billing error is resolved, the following protections apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]:\n\n1. **No collection of disputed amount** — The consumer need not pay, and the creditor may not try to collect, any portion of any required payment the consumer believes is related to the disputed amount (including related finance or other charges). For automatic payment plans, the card issuer shall not deduct any part of the disputed amount or related finance or other charges if a billing error notice is received any time up to **3 business days** before the scheduled payment date.\n\n2. **No adverse credit reports** — The creditor or its agent shall not (directly or indirectly) make or threaten to make an adverse report to any person about the consumer's credit standing, or report that an amount or account is delinquent, because the consumer failed to pay the disputed amount or related finance or other charges.\n\n3. **No acceleration or account restriction** — A creditor shall not accelerate any part of the consumer's indebtedness or restrict or close a consumer's account solely because the consumer has exercised in good faith rights provided by this section. A creditor may be subject to the forfeiture penalty under 15 U.S.C. 1666(e) for failure to comply with any of the requirements of this section.\n\n4. **Permitted creditor actions** — The creditor is not prohibited from: collecting any undisputed portion; deducting the disputed amount and related finance or other charges from the consumer's credit limit; or reflecting the disputed amount on a periodic statement, provided the creditor indicates on or with the periodic statement that payment of the disputed amount and related finance or other charges is not required pending the creditor's compliance with this section.\n\n#### C. Resolution Procedures: If Billing Error Occurred as Asserted\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as asserted, within the time limits of § 1026.13(c)(2), the creditor shall [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]:\n\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related finance or other charges, as applicable; and\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer.\n\n#### D. Resolution Procedures: If No Billing Error or a Different Billing Error Occurred\n\nIf, after conducting a reasonable investigation, the creditor determines no billing error occurred or that a different billing error occurred, within the time limits of § 1026.13(c)(2), the creditor shall [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]:\n\n1. **Mail or deliver an explanation** setting forth the reasons for the creditor's belief that the alleged billing error is incorrect in whole or in part;\n2. **Furnish copies of documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness, if the consumer so requests; and\n3. **If a different billing error occurred**, correct that error and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related finance or other charges, as applicable.\n\n#### E. Creditor's Rights and Duties After Resolution\n\nAfter complying with all requirements, if the creditor determines the consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount and related finance or other charges, the creditor [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]:\n\n1. **Shall promptly notify the consumer in writing** of the time when payment is due and the portion of the disputed amount and related finance or other charges that the consumer still owes.\n2. **Shall allow any grace period** disclosed under §§ 1026.6(a)(1) or (b)(2)(v) and 1026.7(a)(8) or (b)(8) during which the consumer can pay without incurring additional finance or other charges.\n3. **May report the account as delinquent** only after allowing the disclosed grace period or **10 days** (whichever is longer) for the consumer to pay.\n4. **May not report delinquency** if it receives further written notice from the consumer (within the allowed payment period under § 1026.13(g)(3)) that any portion of the billing error is still in dispute, **unless** the creditor also:\n   - Promptly reports that the amount or account is **in dispute**;\n   - Mails or delivers to the consumer (at the same time the report is made) a **written notice of the name and address** of each person to whom the report is made; and\n   - **Promptly reports any subsequent resolution** of the reported delinquency to all persons to whom the creditor made a report. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003] [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\n---\n\n### IV. Reassertion of Billing Error (§ 1026.13(h))\n\nUnder 12 CFR § 1026.13(h), a creditor that has **fully complied** with all of the requirements of § 1026.13 has **no further responsibilities** under this section — other than as provided in § 1026.13(g)(4) (which governs the conditions under which a creditor may report a delinquency when the consumer reasserts a dispute within the allowed payment period) — if a consumer **reasserts substantially the same billing error**. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\n---\n\n### V. Relation to the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E (§ 1026.13(i))\n\n#### A. Regulatory Text: When Regulation E Governs Instead of Regulation Z\n\nUnder 12 CFR § 1026.13(i), a creditor shall comply with the error-resolution requirements of **Regulation E** — specifically 12 CFR 1005.11 and, as applicable, 12 CFR 1005.18(e) — **rather than** the Regulation Z provisions in **§ 1026.13(a), (b), (c), (e), (f), and (h)** in the following two circumstances [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]:\n\n1. **Overdraft and minimum-balance credit lines** — Except with respect to a prepaid account as defined in § 1026.61, an extension of credit that is incident to an electronic fund transfer occurs under an agreement between the consumer and a financial institution to extend credit when the consumer's account is overdrawn or to maintain a specified minimum balance in the consumer's account.\n\n2. **Hybrid prepaid-credit cards** — With regard to a covered separate credit feature and an asset feature of a prepaid account where both are accessible by a hybrid prepaid-credit card as defined in § 1026.61, an extension of credit that is incident to an electronic fund transfer occurs when the hybrid prepaid-credit card accesses both funds in the asset feature of the prepaid account and a credit extension from the credit feature with respect to a particular transaction.\n\nThe regulation specifies that paragraphs **(a), (b), (c), (e), (f), and (h)** of § 1026.13 are displaced in these circumstances. The regulation does not state that paragraphs (d) and (g) of § 1026.13 are displaced. [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\n#### B. Regulation E Error-Resolution Procedures That Apply\n\nWhen Regulation E governs, the following requirements apply under 12 CFR 1005.11:\n\n**Definition of "error" under Regulation E.** Under 12 CFR 1005.11(a)(1), an error includes: an unauthorized EFT; an incorrect EFT to or from the consumer's account; the omission from a periodic statement of an EFT that should have been included; a computational or bookkeeping error made by the financial institution relating to an EFT; the consumer's receipt of an incorrect amount of money from an electronic terminal; an EFT not identified in accordance with the requirements of 12 CFR 1005.9 or 1005.10(a); and a consumer's request for documentation required by 12 CFR 1005.9 or 1005.10(a) or for additional information or clarification concerning an EFT. The term "error" does not include a routine inquiry about the account balance or a request for duplicate copies of documentation made only for tax or other recordkeeping purposes, or the fact that a financial institution does not make a terminal receipt available for a transfer of $15 or less. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0700_chunk_0001]\n\n**Notice of error.** A financial institution must comply with the Regulation E error-resolution procedures with respect to any oral or written notice of error from the consumer that: (1) is received no later than 60 days after the financial institution sends a periodic statement or other documentation first reflecting the alleged error; (2) enables the financial institution to identify the consumer's name and account number; and (3) indicates why the consumer believes the error exists and, to the extent possible, the type, date, and amount of the error. A financial institution may require a consumer to give written confirmation of an error within 10 business days of giving oral notice, and must provide the address where confirmation must be sent. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0700_chunk_0001]\n\n**Investigation and resolution timelines.** After receiving a notice of error, the financial institution must promptly investigate and, under the standard 10-business-day period, determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving the notice, report the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation, and correct the error within one business day after determining that an error occurred. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0700_chunk_0001] [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\nIf the financial institution is unable to complete its investigation within 10 business days, it may take up to 45 days from receipt of the notice to investigate, provided it: (i) provisionally credits the consumer's account in the amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within 10 business days of receiving the error notice (with a permissible withholding of up to $50 if the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a)); (ii) informs the consumer within two business days after the provisional crediting of the amount and date of the provisional credit and gives the consumer full use of the funds during the investigation; (iii) corrects the error, if any, within one business day after determining that an error occurred; and (iv) reports the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation, including notice that a provisional credit has been made final if applicable. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\nThe 10-business-day and 45-day periods are extended in certain circumstances: the applicable time is 20 business days in place of 10 business days if the notice of error involves an EFT to or from the account within 30 days after the first deposit to the account was made; and the applicable time is 90 days in place of 45 days for completing an investigation if the notice of error involves an EFT that was not initiated within a state, resulted from a point-of-sale debit card transaction, or occurred within 30 days after the first deposit to the account was made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\nThe provisional-credit requirement does not apply if the institution requires but does not receive written confirmation within 10 business days of an oral notice of error, or if the alleged error involves an account subject to Regulation T of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Under the amendments, entities making 500 or fewer transfers annually in the current and prior calendar years are not subject to the rule. The Bureau does not intend to cite a violation in an examination or bring an enforcement action against a creditor that takes longer than required by the regulation to resolve a billing error notice, so long as the creditor has made good faith efforts to obtain the necessary information and make a determination as quickly as possible, and complies with all other requirements pending resolution of the error. 83 The statement can be found at: https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_policystatement_remittances-covid-19_2020-04.pdf. 84 The statement can be found at: https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_statement_regulation-zerror-resolution-covid-19_2020-05.pdf."}, {"chunk_id": "12CFR1026_1026.28_chunk_0002", "source": "title_12_part_1026_2026-11-03.xml", "page": "", "rrf_score": 0.025451688923802042, "text": "period for submitting a proper written notice of a billing error under the Federal law.                      ## Electronic Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with error resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer that:\n- Is received **no later than 60 days** after the institution sends the periodic statement reflecting the alleged error [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation\n\n> **Note on $50 withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied § 1005.6(a) requirements, it may withhold a maximum of **$50** from the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must:\n\n- Provide a **written explanation** of its findings\n- **Notify the consumer of their right** to request the documents relied upon in making the determination\n- **Promptly provide those documents** upon request\n- **Reverse any provisional credit** extended during the investigation\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001] CHUNK: 12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002\nCITATION: \nTEXT: equested. (c) Time limits and extent of investigation —(1) Ten-day period. A financial institution shall investigate promptly and, except as otherwise provided in this paragraph (c), shall determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error. The institution shall report the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation. The institution shall correct the error within one business day after determining that an error occurred. (2) Forty-five day period. If the financial institution is unable to complete its investigation within 10 business days, the institution may take up to 45 days from receipt of a notice of error to investigate and determine whether an error occurred, provided the institution does the following: (i) Provisionally credits the consumer's account in the amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within 10 business days of receiving the error notice. If the financial institution has a reasonable basis for believing that an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has occurred and the institution has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), the institution may withhold a maximum of $50 from the amount credited. (ii) Informs the consumer, within two business days after the provisional crediting, of the amount and date of the provisional crediting and gives the consumer full use of the funds during the investigation; (iii) Corrects the error, if any, within one business day after determining that an error occurred; and (iv) Reports the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation (including, if applicable, notice that a provisional credit has been made final). (d) Procedures if financial institution determines no error or different error occurred. The institution's report of the results of its investigation shall include a written explanation of the institution's findings and shall note the consumer's right to request the documents that the institution relied on in making its determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide copies of the documents. (2) Debiting provisional credit. Upon debiting a provisionally credited amount, the financial institution shall: (i) Notify the consumer of the date and amount of the debiting; (ii) Notify the consumer that the institution will honor checks, drafts, or similar instruments payable to third parties and preauthorized transfers from the consumer's account (without charge to the consumer as a result of an overdraft) for five business days after the notification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: same $500 cap as Tier 2\n> - For transfers **after** the 60-day period: **unlimited liability** until the financial institution is notified\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **cannot** impose greater liability based on consumer negligence (e.g., writing a PIN on a card) or a deposit agreement\n- The institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors may not be used\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    CHUNK: 12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001\nCITATION: \nTEXT: (a) Conditions for liability. A consumer may be held liable, within the limitations described in paragraph (b) of this section, for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer involving the consumer's account only if the financial institution has provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3). If the unauthorized transfer involved an access device, it must be an accepted access device and the financial institution must have provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued. (b) Limitations on amount of liability. A consumer's liability for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer or a series of related unauthorized transfers shall be determined as follows: (1) Timely notice given. If the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution. (2) Timely notice not given. If the consumer fails to notify the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $500 or the sum of: (i) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur within the two business days, whichever is less; and (ii) The amount of unauthorized transfers that occur after the close of two business days and before notice to the institution, provided the institution establishes that these transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified the institution within that two-day period. (3) Periodic statement; timely notice not given. A consumer must report an unauthorized electronic fund transfer that appears on a periodic statement within 60 days of the financial institution's transmittal of the statement to avoid liability for subsequent transfers. If the consumer fails to do so, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the amount of the unauthorized transfers that occur after the close of the 60 days and before notice to the institution, and that the institution establishes would not have occurred had the consumer notified the institution within the 60-day period. When an access device is involved in the unauthorized transfer, the consumer may be liable for other amounts set forth in paragraphs (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this section, as applicable. Consumer Liability and Error Resolution Liability of Consumers for Unauthorized Transfers – 12 CFR 1005.6 A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized EFT (defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(m)) depending on when the consumer notifies the financial institution and whether an access device was used to conduct the transaction. Under the EFTA, there is no bright-line time limit within which consumers must report unauthorized EFTs (71 Fed. Reg. 1638, 1653 (Jan. 10, 2006)). The extent of the consumer’s liability is determined solely by the consumer’s promptness in notifying the financial institution (Comment 1005.6(b)-3). Other factors may not be used as a basis to hold consumers liable. Regulation E expressly prohibits the following factors as the basis for imposing greater liability than is permissible under Regulation E: the consumer was negligent (e.g., wrote a PIN on an ATM card); an agreement between the consumer and the financial institution provides for greater liability; or the consumer is liable for a greater amount under state law (Comments 1005.6(b)-2 and 1005.6(b)-3). A consumer may only be held liable for an unauthorized transaction, within the limitations set forth in 12 CFR 1005.6(b), if: • The financial institution has provided all of the following written disclosures to the consumer: o A summary of the consumer’s liability for unauthorized EFTs. o The telephone number and address for reporting that an unauthorized EFT has been or may be made. o The financial institution’s business days. • Any access device used to affect the EFT was an accepted access device (as defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(a)). • The financial institution has provided a means to identify the consumer to whom the access device was issued (12 CFR 1005.6(a)). Regulation E allows, but does not require, the financial institution to provide a separate means to identify each consumer of a multiple-user account (Comment 1005.6(a)-2).                                                                ## Initial Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] Disclosures provided earlier than required (e.g., when a consumer opens a checking account) need not be repeated when the consumer later authorizes an electronic check conversion or agrees to preauthorized transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state/other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The contact information for the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized transfer has been or may be made. A specific telephone number and address must be provided for reporting lost/stolen access devices or possible unauthorized transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Documentation** – A summary of the consumer's right to receipts and periodic statements (per § 1005.9), and notices regarding preauthorized transfers (per § 1005.10(a) and (d)). [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n7. **Stop Payment** – (Referenced in the regulation as a required disclosure, though the full text of this item is truncated in the available evidence.) [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n8. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is also required. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Addition of New EFT Services\n\nIf a **new EFT service** is added to a consumer's account with terms and conditions different from those in the initial disclosures, the financial institution must make new disclosures for that service. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Special Rule for Service Providers\n\nA person that provides EFT services but does not hold the consumer's account must also give the disclosures required by § 1005.7, but only those **within the purview of its relationship with the consumer**. (3) Collection of returned item fees via electronic fund transfer —(i) General. The person initiating an electronic fund transfer to collect a fee for the return of an electronic fund transfer or a check that is unpaid, including due to insufficient or uncollected funds in the consumer's account, must obtain the consumer's authorization for each transfer. A consumer authorizes a one-time electronic fund transfer from his or her account to pay the fee for the returned item or transfer if the person collecting the fee provides notice to the consumer stating that the person may electronically collect the fee, and the consumer goes forward with the underlying transaction. Based on the available evidence, the following framework applies:\n\n---\n\n## Standard Periodic Statement Content\n\nThe evidence references that periodic statements must include the type of information required under **12 CFR 1005.9(b)**, which governs the content of periodic statements for accounts with electronic fund transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n## Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement\n\nThe evidence provides detail on several key exceptions:\n\n### 1. Passbook Accounts\n- Where a consumer's passbook **cannot be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account**, a periodic statement need not be sent\n- Instead, the financial institution must either:\n  - **Update the passbook** (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented), or\n  - **Provide the required information on a separate document** at the consumer's request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 2. Accounts Accessed Only by Preauthorized Transfers\n- For accounts (other than passbook) that may be accessed **only by preauthorized transfers to the account**, the financial institution must send a periodic statement **at least quarterly**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 3. Transfers Between Accounts\n- If a transfer occurs **between two accounts of the same consumer at the same financial institution**, the transfer need only be documented for **one of the two accounts**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 4. Preauthorized Intra-Institutional Transfers\n- A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the same consumer at the same institution is subject to the **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)** rule (preauthorized transfers), **not** the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 5. Foreign-Initiated Transfers\n- Special documentation rules apply when an EFT is initiated outside the United States (evidence is truncated at this point) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n## Alternative to Periodic Statements\n\nA financial institution may provide an **alternative to periodic statements** under **12 CFR 1005.18(b)**, which requires:\n\n- **Account balance** accessible through a readily available telephone line\n- **Electronic history** of account transactions covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account\n- **Written history** of account transactions provided promptly in response to an oral or written request, covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the institution receives the request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.18(b)(1)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\nThe transaction history provided under this alternative must include the **same type of information** required on periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b). [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n### Modified Initial Disclosures Required\nIf using the alternative, the institution must modify its initial disclosures under **12 CFR 1005.7(b)** to include:\n- A telephone number to obtain account balance\n- The means to obtain electronic account history (e.g., website address)\n- A summary of the consumer's right to receive a written account history upon request, including a telephone number to call\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.18(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n## Important Limitation\n\nThe evidence provided does **not include the full text of 12 CFR 1005.9(b)** itself, which contains the complete list of required content items for standard periodic statements. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). For other accounts that may be accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)). • Transfers between accounts. If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- Accelerate the debt or restrict/close the consumer's account solely because the consumer exercised their dispute rights\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines the consumer still owes all or part of the disputed amount, the creditor must promptly notify the consumer in writing of when payment is due and the portion owed.\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. If fees for issuance or availability are optional, these fees should not be considered in determining whether the disclosure must be given. Nonetheless, if the 15 percent threshold test is met, the creditor in providing the disclosure must disclose the amount of available credit calculated by excluding those optional fees, and the available credit including those optional fees. The creditor shall also disclose that the consumer has the right to reject the plan and not be obligated to pay those fees or any other fee or charges until the consumer has used the account or made a payment on the account after receiving a periodic statement. This paragraph does not apply with respect to fees or security deposits that are not debited to the account. (xiv) Web site reference. For issuers of credit cards that are not charge cards, a reference to the Web site established by the Bureau and a statement that consumers may obtain on the Web site information about shopping for and using credit cards. Until January 1, 2013, issuers may substitute for this reference a reference to the Web site established by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. (xv) Billing error rights reference. A statement that information about consumers' right to dispute transactions is included in the account-opening disclosures. (3) Disclosure of charges imposed as part of open-end (not home-secured) plans. A creditor shall disclose, to the extent applicable: (i) For charges imposed as part of an open-end (not home-secured) plan, the circumstances under which the charge may be imposed, including the amount of the charge or an explanation of how the charge is determined. Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. The supplied evidence does not establish the precise consumer notice deadline, so no specific 60-day deadline is asserted here.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note on withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), it may withhold a portion of the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must provide a **written explanation** of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon in making the determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide those documents. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not fully establish all obligations that may apply upon a no-error determination (e.g., reversal of provisional credit), as the relevant regulatory text in the available evidence is truncated.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "equested.                    ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] Consumer Liability and Error Resolution Liability of Consumers for Unauthorized Transfers – 12 CFR 1005.6 A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized EFT (defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(m)) depending on when the consumer notifies the financial institution and whether an access device was used to conduct the transaction.
