                                                                                                                                                                                             ## Initial Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state or other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has been or may be made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] The evidence also indicates that a specific telephone number and address for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the disclosure statement. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is required as part of the initial disclosures. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not include the full text of 12 CFR 1005.9(b) itself. The evidence is insufficient to provide a comprehensive enumeration of all required line items on a standard Regulation E periodic statement.\n\n---\n\n## Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement\n\n### 1. Passbook Accounts\n- Where a consumer's passbook **cannot be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account**, a periodic statement need not be sent\n- Instead, the financial institution must either:\n  - **Update the passbook** (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented), or\n  - **Provide the required information on a separate document** at the consumer's request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 2. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2). Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. For purposes of this section, the term billing error means: (1) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not made to the consumer or to a person who has actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan. (2) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not identified in accordance with the requirements of §§ 1026.7(a)(2) or (b)(2), as applicable, and 1026.8. (4) A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account. (5) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor. (6) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence. (7) The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address if that address was received by the creditor, in writing, at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. The supplied evidence does not establish the precise consumer notice deadline, so no specific 60-day deadline is asserted here.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note on withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), it may withhold a portion of the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must provide a **written explanation** of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon in making the determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide those documents. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not fully establish all obligations that may apply upon a no-error determination (e.g., reversal of provisional credit), as the relevant regulatory text in the available evidence is truncated.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "equested.                    ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] Consumer Liability and Error Resolution Liability of Consumers for Unauthorized Transfers – 12 CFR 1005.6 A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized EFT (defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(m)) depending on when the consumer notifies the financial institution and whether an access device was used to conduct the transaction. Under the EFTA, there is no bright-line time limit within which consumers must report unauthorized EFTs (71 Fed. Reg. 1638, 1653 (Jan. 10, 2006)). The extent of the consumer’s liability is determined solely by the consumer’s promptness in notifying the financial institution (Comment 1005.6(b)-3). Other factors may not be used as a basis to hold consumers liable. Regulation E expressly prohibits the following factors as the basis for imposing greater liability than is permissible under Regulation E: the consumer was negligent (e.g., wrote a PIN on an ATM card); an agreement between the consumer and the financial institution provides for greater liability; or the consumer is liable for a greater amount under state law (Comments 1005.6(b)-2 and 1005.6(b)-3). Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state or other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has been or may be made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] The evidence also indicates that a specific telephone number and address for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the disclosure statement. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is required as part of the initial disclosures. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The available evidence for 12 CFR 1005.7(b) is truncated after the fees item. Additional disclosure items referenced in the regulation (such as documentation rights and stop payment) are not fully reproduced in the available evidence and are therefore not enumerated here.\n\n---\n\n### Addition of New EFT Services\n\nIf a **new EFT service** is added to a consumer's account with terms and conditions different from those described in the initial disclosures, the financial institution must make new disclosures for that service. Based on the available evidence, the following framework applies.\n\n---\n\n## Standard Periodic Statement Content\n\nThe evidence references that periodic statements must include the type of information required under **12 CFR 1005.9(b)**, which governs the content of periodic statements for accounts with electronic fund transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not include the full text of 12 CFR 1005.9(b) itself. Passbook Accounts\n- Where a consumer's passbook **cannot be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account**, a periodic statement need not be sent\n- Instead, the financial institution must either:\n  - **Update the passbook** (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented), or\n  - **Provide the required information on a separate document** at the consumer's request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 2. Accounts Accessed Only by Preauthorized Transfers\n- For accounts (other than passbook) that may be accessed **only by preauthorized transfers to the account**, the financial institution must send a periodic statement **at least quarterly**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 3. Transfers Between Accounts\n- If a transfer occurs **between two accounts of the same consumer at the same financial institution**, the transfer need only be documented for **one of the two accounts**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence also references a rule at 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3) concerning preauthorized intra-institutional transfers, but the relevant text in the evidence is truncated and does not permit a reliable characterization of that rule's content. It is therefore not described here.\n\n---\n\n## Alternative to Periodic Statements\n\nA financial institution may provide an **alternative to periodic statements** under **12 CFR 1005.18(b)**, which requires:\n\n- **Account balance** accessible through a readily available telephone line\n- **Electronic history** of account transactions covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account\n- **Written history** of account transactions provided promptly in response to an oral or written request, covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the institution receives the request\n\nPer **12 CFR 1005.18(b)(1)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\nThe transaction history provided under this alternative must include the **same type of information** required on periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b). [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n### Modified Initial Disclosures Required\nIf using the alternative, the institution must modify its initial disclosures under **12 CFR 1005.7(b)** to include:\n- A telephone number to obtain the account balance\n- The means to obtain an electronic account history (e.g., a website address)\n- A summary of the consumer's right to receive a written account history upon request, including a telephone number to call\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references the specific regulatory subsection governing these modified disclosures but does not reproduce its full citation in a manner that can be independently verified. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). For other accounts that may be accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)). • Transfers between accounts. If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2).                                                                                                                                                                                                      ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. For purposes of this section, the term billing error means: (1) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not made to the consumer or to a person who has actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan. (2) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not identified in accordance with the requirements of §§ 1026.7(a)(2) or (b)(2), as applicable, and 1026.8. (3) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit for property or services not accepted by the consumer or the consumer's designee, or not delivered to the consumer or the consumer's designee as agreed. (4) A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account. (5) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor. (6) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence. (7) The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address if that address was received by the creditor, in writing, at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. (b) Billing error notice. A billing error notice is a written notice from a consumer that: (1) Is received by a creditor at the address disclosed under § 1026.7(a)(9) or (b)(9), as applicable, no later than 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement that reflects the alleged billing error; (2) Enables the creditor to identify the consumer's name and account number; and (3) To the extent possible, indicates the consumer's belief and the reasons for the belief that a billing error exists, and the type, date, and amount of the error. Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. The supplied evidence does not establish the precise consumer notice deadline, so no specific 60-day deadline is asserted here.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note on withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), it may withhold a portion of the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must provide a **written explanation** of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon in making the determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide those documents. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not fully establish all obligations that may apply upon a no-error determination (e.g., reversal of provisional credit), as the relevant regulatory text in the available evidence is truncated.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "equested. (c) Time limits and extent of investigation —(1) Ten-day period. A financial institution shall investigate promptly and, except as otherwise provided in this paragraph (c), shall determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error. The institution shall report the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation. The institution shall correct the error within one business day after determining that an error occurred. (2) Forty-five day period. If the financial institution is unable to complete its investigation within 10 business days, the institution may take up to 45 days from receipt of a notice of error to investigate and determine whether an error occurred, provided the institution does the following: (i) Provisionally credits the consumer's account in the amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within 10 business days of receiving the error notice. (ii) Informs the consumer, within two business days after the provisional crediting, of the amount and date of the provisional crediting and gives the consumer full use of the funds during the investigation; (iii) Corrects the error, if any, within one business day after determining that an error occurred; and (iv) Reports the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation (including, if applicable, notice that a provisional credit has been made final).                                                 ## EFT Error Investigation and Resolution (12 CFR 1005.11)\n\n**Qualifying notice.** The institution must follow error-resolution procedures for any oral or written notice of error received no later than 60 days after it sends the periodic statement first reflecting the alleged error, provided the notice identifies the consumer's name/account number and indicates why an error is believed to exist (12 CFR 1005.11(b)(1)). The institution may require written confirmation of an oral notice within 10 business days (1005.11(b)(2)).\n\n**Standard 10-business-day period (1005.11(c)(1)).** Investigate promptly and determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving the notice; report results to the consumer within 3 business days after completing the investigation; and correct any error within 1 business day after determining it occurred.\n\n**45-day extension (1005.11(c)(2)).** If it cannot finish within 10 business days, the institution may take up to 45 days provided it: (i) provisionally credits the account for the alleged error amount (plus interest where applicable) within 10 business days \u2014 though it may withhold a MAXIMUM of $50 if it has a reasonable basis to believe an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied \u00a7 1005.6(a); (ii) advises the consumer of the provisional credit within 2 business days and gives full use of the funds; (iii) corrects any error within 1 business day of determination; and (iv) reports results within 3 business days of completing the investigation. Provisional credit is NOT required if the institution requires but does not receive written confirmation of an oral notice within 10 business days, or the account is subject to Regulation T.\n\n**Time extensions (1005.11(c)(3)).** 20 business days apply in place of 10 if the notice involves a transfer within 30 days after the first deposit to the account. 90 days apply in place of 45 for completing the investigation if the error involves a transfer that was not initiated within a state, resulted from a point-of-sale debit card transaction, or occurred within 30 days after the first deposit.\n\n**Investigation scope (1005.11(c)(4)).** Except for transfers covered by \u00a7 1005.14, review of the institution's own records suffices if the alleged error concerns a transfer to/from a third party and there is no agreement with that third party for the EFT type involved.\n\n**No error / different error (1005.11(d)).** The institution must provide a written explanation of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon (providing copies promptly on request). If it debits a previously provisional credit, it must (1) notify the consumer of the date and amount of the debit, and (2) honor checks/drafts/preauthorized transfers (without overdraft charge) for 5 business days after notification, to the extent it would have paid them had the credit not been debited. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] Consumer Liability and Error Resolution Liability of Consumers for Unauthorized Transfers – 12 CFR 1005.6 A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized EFT (defined in 12 CFR 1005.2(m)) depending on when the consumer notifies the financial institution and whether an access device was used to conduct the transaction. The framework is tiered.\n\n### Threshold Conditions (12 CFR 1005.6(a))\nA consumer may be held liable only if the financial institution has:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3);\n- Issued an accepted access device; and\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 1 — Notice Within Two Business Days (1005.6(b)(1))\nMaximum liability = lesser of $50 OR the total amount of unauthorized transfers occurring before notice.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 2 — Notice After Two Business Days, Up to 60 Calendar Days (1005.6(b)(2))\nMaximum liability = lesser of $500 OR the sum of: (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is less; AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after the close of two business days and before notice — provided the institution establishes those transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified it within the two-day period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 3 — Notice More Than 60 Calendar Days After Statement Transmittal (1005.6(b)(3))\n- For transfers occurring within the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days.\n- For transfers occurring after the 60-day period: unlimited liability until the financial institution is notified — provided the institution establishes those transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified it within the 60-day period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Extension of Time Limits (1005.6(b)(4))\nIf the consumer's delay in notifying was due to extenuating circumstances, the institution must extend the applicable time periods to a reasonable period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n### Limitations on Imposing Liability\n- A financial institution may impose less liability than Regulation E permits, based on state law or the deposit agreement (1005.6(b)(6)).\n- Liability is determined solely by the consumer's promptness in notifying the institution; consumer negligence, a deposit agreement, or state law may not be used to impose greater liability than Regulation E allows.\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state or other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has been or may be made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] The evidence also indicates that a specific telephone number and address for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the disclosure statement. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is required as part of the initial disclosures. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The available evidence for 12 CFR 1005.7(b) is truncated after the fees item. Additional disclosure items referenced in the regulation (such as documentation rights and stop payment) are not fully reproduced in the available evidence and are therefore not enumerated here.\n\n---\n\n### Addition of New EFT Services\n\nIf a **new EFT service** is added to a consumer's account with terms and conditions different from those described in the initial disclosures, the financial institution must make new disclosures for that service. Liability of consumer \u2013 a summary of the consumer's liability under \u00a7 1005.6 or under state/other applicable law or agreement for unauthorized EFTs. Need not be given if the institution imposes no liability, but must be given before imposing any liability (Comment 1005.7(b)(1)-1).\n2. Telephone number and address \u2013 of the person/office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized EFT has been or may be made (a specific number/address for reporting a lost/stolen access device or possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the statement).\n3. Business days \u2013 the institution's business days.\n4. Types of transfers; limitations \u2013 the types of EFTs the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amount; details may be withheld where confidentiality is essential to system security (but the existence of limitations must still be disclosed).\n5. Fees \u2013 any fees imposed for EFTs or for the right to make transfers.\n6. Documentation \u2013 a summary of the consumer's right to receipts and periodic statements under \u00a7 1005.9 and notices regarding preauthorized transfers under \u00a7 1005.10(a) and (d).\n7. Stop payment \u2013 a summary of the right to stop payment of a preauthorized EFT and the procedure to do so under \u00a7 1005.10(c).\n8. Liability of institution \u2013 a summary of the institution's liability under section 910 of the Act for failure to make or stop certain transfers.\n9. Confidentiality \u2013 the circumstances under which the institution may, in the ordinary course of business, provide account information to third parties.\n10. Error resolution \u2013 a notice substantially similar to Model Form A-3 (Appendix A) concerning error resolution.\n11. ATM fees \u2013 a notice that a fee may be imposed by an ATM operator (\u00a7 1005.16(a)) and by any network used to complete the transaction.\n\nAddition of new EFT services (1005.7(c)): If an EFT service is added with terms and conditions different from those in the initial disclosures, new disclosures for that service are required.\n\nShared systems and service providers: In a shared system, an institution need only make disclosures within its knowledge that apply to its relationship with the consumer for whom it holds an account (12 CFR 1005.4(d)). Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts.    Periodic Statement Requirements Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.9)\n\nGeneral content: Periodic statements must include the same type of information required under 12 CFR 1005.9(b). The full enumeration of required line items is not reproduced in the supplied evidence and cannot be comprehensively stated here.\n\nExceptions to the periodic statement requirement (12 CFR 1005.9(c)):\n- Passbook accounts: Where a consumer's passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, no periodic statement need be sent, provided the institution updates the passbook (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented) or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer's request (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)).\n- Preauthorized-transfer-only accounts: For other (non-passbook) accounts accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)).\n- Transfers between accounts: A transfer between two accounts of the same consumer at the same institution need be documented for only one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two such accounts is subject to the 1005.9(c)(1) preauthorized-transfer rule rather than the 1005.9(c)(2) intra-institutional rule (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)).\n- Foreign-initiated transfers: If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the institution need not provide a receipt or periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)).\n\nAlternative to periodic statements for payroll card accounts (12 CFR 1005.18(b)): An institution may, instead of periodic statements, make available: the account balance through a readily available telephone line; an electronic history of transactions covering at least 60 days preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account; and a written history provided promptly upon oral or written request covering at least 60 days preceding the date of the request (12 CFR 1005.18(b)(1)). This history must include the same type of information required on periodic statements under 1005.9(b) (12 CFR 1005.18(b)(2)).\n\nIf using this alternative, the institution must modify its initial disclosures under 12 CFR 1005.7(b) to include a telephone number to obtain the account balance, the means to obtain an electronic account history (e.g., a website address), and a summary of the consumer's right to receive a written account history upon request including a telephone number to call, plus modified error-resolution notices and annual notices as specified in 12 CFR 1005.18(c).\n\nNote: The retrieved evidence does not reproduce the full line-item content requirements of 12 CFR 1005.9(a)/(b); those specific required disclosures cannot be enumerated from the supplied evidence. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

                                                                                                                                                                                                     ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. An extension of credit not made to the consumer or a person with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account.\n2. An extension of credit not identified in accordance with §§ 1026.7(a)(2)/(b)(2) and 1026.8.\n3. A charge for property/services not accepted by the consumer (or designee) or not delivered as agreed.\n4. The creditor's failure to credit a payment or other credit properly.\n5. A computational or similar accounting error made by the creditor.\n6. An extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence.\n7. The creditor's failure to mail/deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle.\n\n### What Makes a Billing-Error Notice 'Proper' [1026.13(b)]\nA billing-error notice must be a written notice that: (1) is received at the disclosed address no later than 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement reflecting the alleged error; (2) enables the creditor to identify the consumer's name and account number; and (3) to the extent possible, states the consumer's belief, the reasons for it, and the type, date, and amount of the error.\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Proper Notice\nTime limits [1026.13(c)]: The creditor must mail/deliver written acknowledgment within 30 days of receipt (unless it resolves the matter within that period), and must comply with the resolution procedures of paragraphs (e) or (f) within two complete billing cycles, but no later than 90 days, after receiving the notice.\n\nRules pending resolution [1026.13(d)]:\n- The consumer need not pay, and the creditor may not try to collect, the disputed amount (including related finance/other charges). For automatic payment plans, the issuer must not deduct the disputed amount if the notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date.\n- No adverse credit reports (directly or indirectly) based on nonpayment of the disputed amount.\n- No acceleration of the indebtedness or restricting/closing the account solely because the consumer exercised these rights in good faith; noncompliance may trigger the forfeiture penalty under 15 U.S.C. 1666(e).\n- Permitted: collecting any undisputed portion, deducting the disputed amount from the credit limit, and reflecting the disputed amount on the statement if it indicates payment is not required pending compliance.\n\nIf the billing error occurred as asserted [1026.13(e)]: Within the (c)(2) time limits, correct the error, credit the account with the disputed amount and related finance/other charges, and mail/deliver a correction notice.\n\nIf no error, or a different error, occurred [1026.13(f)]: Within the (c)(2) time limits, mail/deliver an explanation of the reasons the alleged error is incorrect in whole or part; furnish copies of documentary evidence of indebtedness if requested; and if a different error occurred, correct it and credit the account accordingly.\n\nAfter resolution, if the consumer still owes [1026.13(g)]: Promptly notify the consumer in writing of the amount still owed and when payment is due; allow any disclosed grace period for payment without additional charges; the creditor may report the amount as delinquent only after allowing the disclosed period or 10 days (whichever is longer); and if the consumer re-disputes in writing within the allowed period, the creditor may not report delinquency unless it also promptly reports the dispute, notifies the consumer of recipients of the report, and reports any subsequent resolution.\n\nReassertion [1026.13(h)]: A creditor that has fully complied has no further responsibilities (other than under (g)(4)) if the consumer reasserts substantially the same error.\n\nRelation to Regulation E [1026.13(i)]: If the credit extension is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit or certain hybrid prepaid-credit card transactions), the creditor must follow Regulation E error-resolution procedures (12 CFR 1005.11, 1005.18(e)) instead of paragraphs (a), (b), (c), (e), (f), and (h). us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3.                                                 ## EFT Error Investigation and Resolution (12 CFR 1005.11)\n\n**Qualifying notice.** The institution must follow error-resolution procedures for any oral or written notice of error received no later than 60 days after it sends the periodic statement first reflecting the alleged error, provided the notice identifies the consumer's name/account number and indicates why an error is believed to exist (12 CFR 1005.11(b)(1)). The institution may require written confirmation of an oral notice within 10 business days (1005.11(b)(2)).\n\n**Standard 10-business-day period (1005.11(c)(1)).** Investigate promptly and determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving the notice; report results to the consumer within 3 business days after completing the investigation; and correct any error within 1 business day after determining it occurred.\n\n**45-day extension (1005.11(c)(2)).** If it cannot finish within 10 business days, the institution may take up to 45 days provided it: (i) provisionally credits the account for the alleged error amount (plus interest where applicable) within 10 business days \u2014 though it may withhold a MAXIMUM of $50 if it has a reasonable basis to believe an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied \u00a7 1005.6(a); (ii) advises the consumer of the provisional credit within 2 business days and gives full use of the funds; (iii) corrects any error within 1 business day of determination; and (iv) reports results within 3 business days of completing the investigation. Provisional credit is NOT required if the institution requires but does not receive written confirmation of an oral notice within 10 business days, or the account is subject to Regulation T.\n\n**Time extensions (1005.11(c)(3)).** 20 business days apply in place of 10 if the notice involves a transfer within 30 days after the first deposit to the account. 90 days apply in place of 45 for completing the investigation if the error involves a transfer that was not initiated within a state, resulted from a point-of-sale debit card transaction, or occurred within 30 days after the first deposit.\n\n**Investigation scope (1005.11(c)(4)).** Except for transfers covered by \u00a7 1005.14, review of the institution's own records suffices if the alleged error concerns a transfer to/from a third party and there is no agreement with that third party for the EFT type involved.\n\n**No error / different error (1005.11(d)).** The institution must provide a written explanation of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon (providing copies promptly on request). If it debits a previously provisional credit, it must (1) notify the consumer of the date and amount of the debit, and (2) honor checks/drafts/preauthorized transfers (without overdraft charge) for 5 business days after notification, to the extent it would have paid them had the credit not been debited. us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

                   ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] The framework is tiered.\n\n### Threshold Conditions (12 CFR 1005.6(a))\nA consumer may be held liable only if the financial institution has:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3);\n- Issued an accepted access device; and\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 1 — Notice Within Two Business Days (1005.6(b)(1))\nMaximum liability = lesser of $50 OR the total amount of unauthorized transfers occurring before notice.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 2 — Notice After Two Business Days, Up to 60 Calendar Days (1005.6(b)(2))\nMaximum liability = lesser of $500 OR the sum of: (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is less; AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after the close of two business days and before notice — provided the institution establishes those transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified it within the two-day period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Tier 3 — Notice More Than 60 Calendar Days After Statement Transmittal (1005.6(b)(3))\n- For transfers occurring within the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days.\n- For transfers occurring after the 60-day period: unlimited liability until the financial institution is notified — provided the institution establishes those transfers would not have occurred had the consumer notified it within the 60-day period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n### Extension of Time Limits (1005.6(b)(4))\nIf the consumer's delay in notifying was due to extenuating circumstances, the institution must extend the applicable time periods to a reasonable period.\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n### Limitations on Imposing Liability\n- A financial institution may impose less liability than Regulation E permits, based on state law or the deposit agreement (1005.6(b)(6)).\n- Liability is determined solely by the consumer's promptness in notifying the institution; consumer negligence, a deposit agreement, or state law may not be used to impose greater liability than Regulation E allows.\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 LLM_JUDGE_REVIEWED

                                                                                                                                                                                             ## Initial Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state or other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has been or may be made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] The evidence also indicates that a specific telephone number and address for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the disclosure statement. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is required as part of the initial disclosures. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The available evidence for 12 CFR 1005.7(b) is truncated after the fees item. Additional disclosure items referenced in the regulation (such as documentation rights and stop payment) are not fully reproduced in the available evidence and are therefore not enumerated here.\n\n---\n\n### Addition of New EFT Services\n\nIf a **new EFT service** is added to a consumer's account with terms and conditions different from those described in the initial disclosures, the financial institution must make new disclosures for that service. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Special Rule for Service Providers\n\nA person that provides EFT services but does not hold the consumer's account must also give the disclosures required by § 1005.7, but only those **within the purview of its relationship with the consumer**.
