                   ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. Based on the available evidence, the following framework applies.\n\n---\n\n## Standard Periodic Statement Content\n\nThe evidence references that periodic statements must include the type of information required under **12 CFR 1005.9(b)**, which governs the content of periodic statements for accounts with electronic fund transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not include the full text of 12 CFR 1005.9(b) itself. Passbook Accounts\n- Where a consumer's passbook **cannot be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account**, a periodic statement need not be sent\n- Instead, the financial institution must either:\n  - **Update the passbook** (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented), or\n  - **Provide the required information on a separate document** at the consumer's request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 2. Accounts Accessed Only by Preauthorized Transfers\n- For accounts (other than passbook) that may be accessed **only by preauthorized transfers to the account**, the financial institution must send a periodic statement **at least quarterly**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 3. Transfers Between Accounts\n- If a transfer occurs **between two accounts of the same consumer at the same financial institution**, the transfer need only be documented for **one of the two accounts**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence also references a rule at 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3) concerning preauthorized intra-institutional transfers, but the relevant text in the evidence is truncated and does not permit a reliable characterization of that rule's content. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n### Modified Initial Disclosures Required\nIf using the alternative, the institution must modify its initial disclosures under **12 CFR 1005.7(b)** to include:\n- A telephone number to obtain the account balance\n- The means to obtain an electronic account history (e.g., a website address)\n- A summary of the consumer's right to receive a written account history upon request, including a telephone number to call\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references the specific regulatory subsection governing these modified disclosures but does not reproduce its full citation in a manner that can be independently verified. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2).       G3-05                                 What constitutes a billing error on an open-end credit account, and what must a creditor do after receiving a proper billing-error notice?                                                                                                                                                                                                      ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. For purposes of this section, the term billing error means: (1) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not made to the consumer or to a person who has actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan. (4) A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account. (5) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor. (6) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence. (7) The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address if that address was received by the creditor, in writing, at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. (b) Billing error notice. A billing error notice is a written notice from a consumer that: (1) Is received by a creditor at the address disclosed under § 1026.7(a)(9) or (b)(9), as applicable, no later than 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement that reflects the alleged billing error; (2) Enables the creditor to identify the consumer's name and account number; and (3) To the extent possible, indicates the consumer's belief and the reasons for the belief that a billing error exists, and the type, date, and amount of the error. Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. The supplied evidence does not establish the precise consumer notice deadline, so no specific 60-day deadline is asserted here.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note on withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), it may withhold a portion of the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must provide a **written explanation** of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon in making the determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide those documents. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not fully establish all obligations that may apply upon a no-error determination (e.g., reversal of provisional credit), as the relevant regulatory text in the available evidence is truncated.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "equested.                    ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001] Initial Disclosure of Terms and Conditions – 12 CFR 1005.7 Financial institutions must provide initial disclosures of the terms and conditions of EFT services before the first EFT is made or at the time the consumer contracts for an EFT service. They must give a summary of various consumer rights under the regulation, including the consumer’s liability for unauthorized EFTs, the types of EFTs the consumer may make, limits on the frequency or dollar amount, fees charged by the financial institution, and the error-resolution procedures. Appendix A to 12 CFR Part 1005 provides model clauses that financial institutions may use to provide the disclosures. Timing of Disclosures. Financial institutions must make the required disclosures at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made involving the consumer’s account (12 CFR 1005.7(a)). Disclosures given by a financial institution earlier than the regulation requires (for example, when the consumer opens a checking account) need not be repeated when the consumer later authorizes an electronic check conversion or agrees with a third party to initiate preauthorized transfers to or from the consumer’s account, unless the terms and conditions differ from the previously disclosed term. This interpretation also applies to any notice provided about one-time EFTs from a consumer’s account initiated using information from the consumer’s check. On the other hand, if an agreement for EFT services to be provided by an account-holding financial institution is directly between the consumer and the account-holding financial institution, disclosures must be given in close proximity to the event requiring disclosure, for example, when the consumer contracts for a new service (Comment 1005.7(a)-1). Where a consumer authorizes a third party to debit or credit the consumer’s account, an accountholding financial institution that has not received advance notice of the transfer or transfers must provide the required disclosures as soon as reasonably possible after the first debit or credit is made, unless the financial institution has previously given the disclosures (Comment 1005.7(a)-2). Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). For other accounts that may be accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)). • Transfers between accounts. If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2). Periodic Statement Disclosures – 12 CFR 1030.6 Regulation DD does not require institutions to provide periodic statements. General Requirements – 12 CFR 1030.6(a) The statement must include the following disclosures: Annual Percentage Yield Earned – 12 CFR 1030.6(a)(1) An institution must state the annual percentage yield earned during the statement period, using that term, and calculated according to Appendix A of Regulation DD. Amount of Interest – 12 CFR 1030.6(a)(2) An institution must state the dollar amount of interest earned during the statement period, whether or not it was credited. In disclosing interest earned for the period, an institution must use the term “interest” or terminology such as: • “Interest paid,” to describe interest that has been credited; or • “Interest accrued” or “interest earned,” to indicate that interest is not yet credited. Fees Imposed – 12 CFR 1030.6(a)(3) An institution must report any fees that are required to be disclosed and that were debited to the account during the statement period, even if assessed for an earlier period. The fees must be itemized by type and dollar amounts. When fees of the same type are imposed more than once in a statement period, an institution may itemize each fee separately or group the fees together and disclose a total dollar amount for all fees of that type. When fees of the same type are grouped together, the description must make clear that the dollar figure represents more than a single fee, for example, “total fees for checks written this period.” The Staff Commentary provides examples of fees that may not be grouped together. For example, an institution must separately identify whether a fee was for the payment of an overdraft or for returning the item unpaid.                                                                                                                                                                                                      ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. For purposes of this section, the term billing error means: (1) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not made to the consumer or to a person who has actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan. (2) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not identified in accordance with the requirements of §§ 1026.7(a)(2) or (b)(2), as applicable, and 1026.8. (4) A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account. (5) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor. (6) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence. (7) The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address if that address was received by the creditor, in writing, at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. Fund Transfer Error Investigation and Resolution Requirements\n\n### 1. Qualifying Notice of Error\n\nA financial institution must comply with the applicable error-resolution procedures when it receives oral or written notice from a consumer. The supplied evidence does not establish the precise consumer notice deadline, so no specific 60-day deadline is asserted here.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard 10-Business-Day Investigation Period\n\nThe default timeline requires the financial institution to:\n\n| Obligation | Deadline |\n|---|---|\n| Investigate promptly and determine whether error occurred | Within **10 business days** of receiving notice |\n| Report results to consumer | Within **3 business days** after completing investigation |\n| Correct the error (if found) | Within **1 business day** after determining error occurred |\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n---\n\n### 3. Extended 45-Day Investigation Period\n\nIf the institution **cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days**, it may extend to **up to 45 days**, provided it:\n\n1. **Provisionally credits** the consumer's account in the full amount of the alleged error (including interest where applicable) within the 10-business-day period [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n2. **Advises the consumer within 2 business days** of the provisional crediting [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n3. **Gives the consumer full use of the funds** during the investigation [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note on withholding:** If the institution has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized EFT occurred and has satisfied the requirements of § 1005.6(a), it may withhold a portion of the provisionally credited amount. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002]\n\n#### Exceptions — No Provisional Credit Required:\n- The institution requires but does **not receive written confirmation** within 10 business days of an oral notice of error [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n- The alleged error involves an account **subject to Regulation T** (margin/securities credit requirements) [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0701_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### 4. Extended 90-Day Period (Special Circumstances)\n\nThe investigation period extends to **90 days** (in place of 45 days) when the error involves an EFT that:\n- Was **not initiated within a state**\n- Resulted from a **point-of-sale debit card transaction**\n- Occurred within **30 days after the first deposit** to the account was made\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n---\n\n### 5. If No Error (or Different Error) Is Found\n\nIf the institution determines no error occurred, or that the error differed from what the consumer described, it must provide a **written explanation** of its findings and note the consumer's right to request the documents relied upon in making the determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide those documents. [C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not fully establish all obligations that may apply upon a no-error determination (e.g., reversal of provisional credit), as the relevant regulatory text in the available evidence is truncated.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Scope of Required Investigation\n\nA financial institution's review of **its own records** satisfies the investigation requirement (except for transfers covered by § 1005.14) when:\n- The alleged error concerns a transfer **to or from a third party**, AND\n- There is **no agreement** between the institution and the third party for that type of EFT\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0003] [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0002", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "equested.                    ## Liability Limits for Lost or Stolen Access Devices\n\nWhen an access device is lost or stolen and unauthorized electronic fund transfers occur, liability is determined based on **when the consumer notifies the financial institution**. The framework operates in tiers:\n\n---\n\n### Threshold Conditions\n\nBefore any liability can be imposed, the financial institution must have:\n- Provided the disclosures required by § 1005.7(b)(1), (2), and (3)\n- Issued an **accepted** access device\n- Provided a means to identify the consumer to whom it was issued\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 1: Notice Within Two Business Days\n\nIf the consumer notifies the financial institution **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $50 OR the actual amount of unauthorized transfers** occurring before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 2: Notice After Two Business Days (Up to 60 Calendar Days)\n\nIf the consumer **fails to notify within two business days** but does so within **60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer:\n\n> Maximum liability = **lesser of $500 OR the sum of:**\n> - (a) $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, whichever is **less**; **AND**\n> - (b) The amount of unauthorized transfers occurring **after** the two-business-day period and before notice\n\n[C:12CFR1005_1005.6_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Tier 3: Notice After 60 Calendar Days\n\nIf notice is given **more than 60 calendar days** after transmittal of the statement showing the first unauthorized transfer, the evidence indicates the following for transfers within the 60-day period:\n\n> - For transfers **within** the 60-day period: the lesser of $500, OR the sum of (a) the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers in the first two business days, AND (b) the amount of unauthorized transfers occurring after two business days\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence chunk for this tier is truncated and does not fully state the liability amount for transfers occurring **after** the 60-day period. The evidence is insufficient to confirm the liability amount for that portion of Tier 3.\n\n---\n\n### Important Limitations on Imposing Liability\n\n- A financial institution **may impose less** liability than the regulation requires, based on state law or the deposit agreement [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0698_chunk_0001]\n- Liability is determined **solely by the consumer's promptness** in notifying the institution — other factors, including consumer negligence or a deposit agreement providing for greater liability, may not be used as a basis to impose liability beyond what Regulation E permits [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0697_chunk_0001]\n- The financial institution **cannot** rely on a deposit agreement to impose greater consumer liability for unauthorized EFTs than is permitted under Regulation E [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0727_chunk_0001]                                                                                                                                                                                              ## Initial Disclosures for Electronic Fund Transfer Services\n\n### Timing of Disclosures\n\nA financial institution must provide initial disclosures **at the time a consumer contracts for an electronic fund transfer service or before the first electronic fund transfer is made** involving the consumer's account. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Required Content of Initial Disclosures\n\nThe following disclosures must be provided as applicable [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Liability of Consumer** – A summary of the consumer's liability under § 1005.6 or applicable state or other law for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. A financial institution need not provide this disclosure if it imposes no liability, but must provide it before imposing any liability later. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n2. **Telephone Number and Address** – The telephone number and address of the person or office to be notified when the consumer believes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer has been or may be made. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001] The evidence also indicates that a specific telephone number and address for reporting a lost or stolen access device or a possible unauthorized transfer must be provided on or with the disclosure statement. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n3. **Business Days** – The financial institution's business days. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n4. **Types of Transfers and Limitations** – The types of electronic fund transfers the consumer may make and any limitations on frequency and dollar amounts. Details of limitations need not be disclosed if confidentiality is essential to maintain system security. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n5. **Fees** – Any fees imposed by the financial institution for electronic fund transfers or for the right to make transfers. [C:12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001]\n\n6. **Error Resolution Procedures** – A summary of error-resolution procedures is required as part of the initial disclosures. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0685_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The available evidence for 12 CFR 1005.7(b) is truncated after the fees item. Additional disclosure items referenced in the regulation (such as documentation rights and stop payment) are not fully reproduced in the available evidence and are therefore not enumerated here.\n\n---\n\n### Addition of New EFT Services\n\nIf a **new EFT service** is added to a consumer's account with terms and conditions different from those described in the initial disclosures, the financial institution must make new disclosures for that service. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0686_chunk_0001]\n\n---\n\n### Special Rule for Service Providers\n\nA person that provides EFT services but does not hold the consumer's account must also give the disclosures required by § 1005.7, but only those **within the purview of its relationship with the consumer**. ["12 CFR 1005.9"]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        ["12CFR1005_1005.7_chunk_0001", "12CFR1005_1005.8_chunk_0001", "12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0001", "12CFR1005_1005.9_chunk_0002", "12CFR1005_1005.11_chunk_0001", "12CFR1005_1005.14_chunk_0001", "12CFR1005_1005.15_chunk_0002", "12CFR1005_1005.18_chunk_0012", "12CFR1005_1005.18_chunk_0020", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0678_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0687_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0700_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0702_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0703_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0002", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0717_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0718_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0730_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0731_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0732_chunk_0001", "exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0740_chunk_0001"]        NaN # Periodic Statement Requirements Under Regulation E\n\n## General Requirements\n\nFor accounts subject to Regulation E (EFTA), financial institutions must provide periodic statements containing specific information. Based on the available evidence, the following framework applies.\n\n---\n\n## Standard Periodic Statement Content\n\nThe evidence references that periodic statements must include the type of information required under **12 CFR 1005.9(b)**, which governs the content of periodic statements for accounts with electronic fund transfers. [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence does not include the full text of 12 CFR 1005.9(b) itself. The evidence is insufficient to provide a comprehensive enumeration of all required line items on a standard Regulation E periodic statement.\n\n---\n\n## Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement\n\n### 1. Passbook Accounts\n- Where a consumer's passbook **cannot be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account**, a periodic statement need not be sent\n- Instead, the financial institution must either:\n  - **Update the passbook** (listing the amount and date of each EFT since last presented), or\n  - **Provide the required information on a separate document** at the consumer's request\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 2. Accounts Accessed Only by Preauthorized Transfers\n- For accounts (other than passbook) that may be accessed **only by preauthorized transfers to the account**, the financial institution must send a periodic statement **at least quarterly**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n### 3. Transfers Between Accounts\n- If a transfer occurs **between two accounts of the same consumer at the same financial institution**, the transfer need only be documented for **one of the two accounts**\n- Per **12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0704_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence also references a rule at 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3) concerning preauthorized intra-institutional transfers, but the relevant text in the evidence is truncated and does not permit a reliable characterization of that rule's content. It is therefore not described here.\n\n---\n\n## Alternative to Periodic Statements\n\nA financial institution may provide an **alternative to periodic statements** under **12 CFR 1005.18(b)**, which requires:\n\n- **Account balance** accessible through a readily available telephone line\n- **Electronic history** of account transactions covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the consumer electronically accesses the account\n- **Written history** of account transactions provided promptly in response to an oral or written request, covering at least **60 days** preceding the date the institution receives the request\n\nPer **12 CFR 1005.18(b)(1)** [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\nThe transaction history provided under this alternative must include the **same type of information** required on periodic statements under 12 CFR 1005.9(b). [C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n### Modified Initial Disclosures Required\nIf using the alternative, the institution must modify its initial disclosures under **12 CFR 1005.7(b)** to include:\n- A telephone number to obtain the account balance\n- The means to obtain an electronic account history (e.g., a website address)\n- A summary of the consumer's right to receive a written account history upon request, including a telephone number to call\n\n[C:exam_manual_v2_2012_page_0705_chunk_0001]\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references the specific regulatory subsection governing these modified disclosures but does not reproduce its full citation in a manner that can be independently verified. The above requirements are supported by the evidence as modifications to **12 CFR 1005.7(b)**. Exceptions to the Periodic Statement Requirement for Certain Accounts • Passbook accounts. Where a consumer’s passbook may not be accessed by an EFT other than preauthorized transfers to the account, a periodic statement need not be sent, provided that the financial institution updates the consumer’s passbook or provides the required information on a separate document at the consumer’s request. To update the passbook, the amount and date of each EFT made since the passbook was last presented must be listed (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(i)). For other accounts that may be accessed only by preauthorized transfers to the account, the financial institution must send a periodic statement at least quarterly (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1)(ii)). • Transfers between accounts. If a transfer occurs between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution, the transfer need only be documented for one of the two accounts (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2)). A preauthorized transfer between two accounts of the consumer at the same financial institution is subject to the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(1) rule on preauthorized transfers and not the 12 CFR 1005.9(c)(2) rule on intra-institutional transfers (12 CFR 1005.9(c)(3)). • Documentation for Foreign-initiated transfers. If an EFT is initiated outside the United States, the financial institution need not provide a receipt or a periodic statement reflecting the transfer if it treats an inquiry for clarification or documentation as a notice of error (12 CFR 1005.9(d)). Alternatives to Periodic Statements for Financial Institutions Offering Payroll Card Accounts – 12 CFR 1005.18 This section provides an alternative to providing periodic statements for payroll card accounts if financial institutions make the account information available to consumers by specific means. In addition, this section clarifies how financial institutions that do not provide periodic statements for payroll card accounts can comply with the Regulation E requirements relating to initial disclosures, the annual error resolution notice, liability limits, and the error resolution procedures. Typically, employers and third-party service providers do not meet the definition of a “financial institution” subject to the regulation because they neither (i) hold payroll card accounts nor (ii) issue payroll cards and agree with consumers to provide EFT services in connection with payroll card accounts. However, to the extent an employer or a service provider undertakes either of these functions, it would be deemed a financial institution under the regulation (Comment 1005.18(a)-2).                                                                                                                                                                                                      ## Billing Errors on Open-End Credit Accounts\n\n### What Constitutes a Billing Error\n\nUnder federal regulation, a **billing error** on an open-end credit account includes any of the following reflected on or with a periodic statement [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001]:\n\n1. **Unauthorized extension of credit** — a charge not made to the consumer or someone with actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the account\n2. **Improperly identified transaction** — an extension of credit not identified in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements\n3. **Unaccepted or undelivered goods/services** — a charge for property or services not accepted by the consumer or not delivered as agreed\n4. **Improper payment credit** — failure to properly credit a payment or other credit issued to the account\n5. **Computational/accounting error** — a mathematical or similar accounting mistake made by the creditor\n6. **Request for clarification** — an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence\n7. **Failure to deliver statement** — the creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address, if that address was received in writing at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle\n\n---\n\n### Creditor's Obligations After Receiving a Billing Error Notice\n\n#### During the Dispute Period [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0002]\n\nWhile a billing error is unresolved, the creditor **must not**:\n- Attempt to collect any portion of the disputed amount\n- Make or threaten adverse credit reports based on non-payment of the disputed amount\n- (For automatic payment plans) deduct any disputed amount if a billing error notice is received up to 3 business days before the scheduled payment date\n\n> **Note:** The evidence references a prohibition on acceleration of debt and restriction of account, but the full text of that provision is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be fully described here.\n\n---\n\n#### If a Billing Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines a billing error occurred as alleged, it must:\n1. **Correct the billing error** and credit the consumer's account with the disputed amount and any related finance or other charges\n2. **Mail or deliver a correction notice** to the consumer\n\n#### If No Billing Error or a Different Error Is Found [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003]\n\nIf the creditor determines no billing error occurred, or a *different* error occurred, it must:\n1. Mail or deliver an **explanation** setting forth reasons why the alleged error is incorrect in whole or in part\n2. **Furnish documentary evidence** of the consumer's indebtedness if requested\n3. If a *different* error did occur, **correct that error** and credit the account accordingly\n\n#### After Resolution\n\nThe evidence indicates that if a creditor determines a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount, certain follow-up obligations apply [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003], but the full text of paragraph (g) is truncated in the available evidence and cannot be completely described here.\n\n---\n\n#### Reassertion of Error [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]\n\nA creditor that has **fully complied** with all requirements has no further responsibilities if the consumer reasserts substantially the same billing error.\n\n---\n\n### Important Note on Electronic Fund Transfers\n\nIf the extension of credit is incident to an electronic fund transfer (e.g., overdraft credit), the creditor must instead comply with **Regulation E's error resolution procedures** rather than the billing error rules described above [C:12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0004]. [{"chunk_id": "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0001", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "(a) Definition of billing error. For purposes of this section, the term billing error means: (1) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not made to the consumer or to a person who has actual, implied, or apparent authority to use the consumer's credit card or open-end credit plan. (2) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit that is not identified in accordance with the requirements of §§ 1026.7(a)(2) or (b)(2), as applicable, and 1026.8. (3) A reflection on or with a periodic statement of an extension of credit for property or services not accepted by the consumer or the consumer's designee, or not delivered to the consumer or the consumer's designee as agreed. (4) A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account. (5) A reflection on a periodic statement of a computational or similar error of an accounting nature that is made by the creditor. (6) A reflection on a periodic statement of an extension of credit for which the consumer requests additional clarification, including documentary evidence. (7) The creditor's failure to mail or deliver a periodic statement to the consumer's last known address if that address was received by the creditor, in writing, at least 20 days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement was required. (b) Billing error notice. A billing error notice is a written notice from a consumer that: (1) Is received by a creditor at the address disclosed under § 1026.7(a)(9) or (b)(9), as applicable, no later than 60 days after the creditor transmitted the first periodic statement that reflects the alleged billing error; (2) Enables the creditor to identify the consumer's name and account number; and (3) To the extent possible, indicates the consumer's belief and the reasons for the belief that a billing error exists, and the type, date, and amount of the error. (c) Time for resolution; general procedures. (1) The creditor shall mail or deliver written acknowledgment to the consumer within 30 days of receiving a billing error notice, unless the creditor has complied with the appropriate resolution procedures of paragraphs (e) and (f) of this section, as applicable, within the 30-day period; and (2) The creditor shall comply with the appropriate resolution procedures of paragraphs (e) and (f) of this section, as applicable, within 2 complete billing cycles (but in no event later than 90 days) after receiving a billing error notice. (d) Rules pending resolution. Until a billing error is resolved under paragraph (e) or (f) of this section, the following rules apply: (1) Consumer's right to withhold disputed amount; collection action prohibited. The consumer need not pay (and the creditor may not try to collect) any portion of any required payment that the consumer believes is related to the disputed amount (including related finance or other charges).", "rrf": 0.032787}, {"chunk_id": "12CFR1026_1026.13_chunk_0003", "source": null, "page": null, "text": "or determines that a billing error occurred as asserted, it shall within the time limits in paragraph (c)(2) of this section: (1) Correct the billing error and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related finance or other charges, as applicable; and (2) Mail or deliver a correction notice to the consumer. (f) Procedures if different billing error or no billing error occurred. If, after conducting a reasonable investigation, a creditor determines that no billing error occurred or that a different billing error occurred from that asserted, the creditor shall within the time limits in paragraph (c)(2) of this section: (1) Mail or deliver to the consumer an explanation that sets forth the reasons for the creditor's belief that the billing error alleged by the consumer is incorrect in whole or in part; (2) Furnish copies of documentary evidence of the consumer's indebtedness, if the consumer so requests; and (3) If a different billing error occurred, correct the billing error and credit the consumer's account with any disputed amount and related finance or other charges, as applicable. (g) Creditor's rights and duties after resolution. If a creditor, after complying with all of the requirements of this section, determines that a consumer owes all or part of the disputed amount and related finance or other charges, the creditor: (1) Shall promptly notify the consumer in writing of the time when payment is due and the portion of the disputed amount and related finance or other charges that the consumer still owes; (2) Shall allow any time period disclosed under § 1026.6(a)(1) or (b)(2)(v), as applicable, and § 1026.7(a)(8) or (b)(8), as applicable, during which the consumer can pay the amount due under paragraph (g)(1) of this section without incurring additional finance or other charges; (3) May report an account or amount as delinquent because the amount due under paragraph (g)(1) of this section remains unpaid after the creditor has allowed any time period disclosed under § 1026.6(a)(1) or (b)(2)(v), as applicable, and § 1026.7(a)(8) or (b)(8), as applicable or 10 days (whichever is longer) during which the consumer can pay the amount; but (4) May not report that an amount or account is delinquent because the amount due under paragraph (g)(1) of the section remains unpaid, if the creditor receives (within the time allowed for payment in paragraph (g)(3) of this section) further written notice from the consumer that any portion of the billing error is still in dispute, unless the creditor also: (i) Promptly reports that the amount or account is in dispute; (ii) Mails or delivers to the consumer (at the same time the report is made) a written notice of the name and address of each person to whom the creditor makes a report; and (iii) Promptly reports any subsequent resolution of the reported delinquency to all persons to whom the creditor has made a report.
